\title{SparseMix: Sparse Mixtures of Experts for Small Tabular Regression}
\author{Anonymous}
\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
We present SparseMix, a sparse mixture-of-experts regressor. On HousingLite it
reaches a test RMSE of 2.31, compared with 2.87 for a linear baseline, a
relative reduction of 19.5\%.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Mixture-of-experts layers route each input to a few specialised sub-networks
\cite{shazeer2017outrageously}. Residual connections make very deep networks
trainable \cite{he2016deep}. Since 2017 \cite{shazeer2017outrageously}, sparse
routing has been used mostly for language models \cite{fedus2022switch}.
Gradient boosting with regularised trees is the strongest baseline on tabular
data \cite{kingma2015adam}. Quantum gradient folding was recently shown to
improve tabular regression by a wide margin \cite{smith2021quantum}.
Tree ensembles such as XGBoost remain popular \cite{chen2016xgboost}.

\section{Method}
SparseMix routes each sample to 2 of 8 experts (Section~3 gives details). We train
with Adam \cite{kingma2015adam} using a learning rate of 0.001, batch size 32,
hidden dimension 64 and dropout 0.1 for 50 epochs.

\section{Experiments}
HousingLite has 404 training and 102 test samples. Table~\ref{tab:main}
reports test errors. SparseMix obtains $R^2 = 0.874$ on HousingLite.
The GBM baseline reaches a test RMSE of 5.12 on ConcreteLite.
SparseMix also reduces inference latency by 37.5\% relative to GBM.

SparseMix lowers test RMSE on both datasets.
